title: W3C Internationalization Working Group-relevant MDN issues
description: Issue filed on MDN Web Docs related to pages attached to technologies developed by W3C Internationalization Working Group

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/TextDecoder

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Examples section, "Representing text with typed arrays" subsection

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The "Representing text with typed arrays" example only lists Uint8Array, Int8Array, Uint16Array, Int16Array, and Int32Array.

It omits Uint32Array, and does not mention that TextDecoder.decode() accepts any BufferSource, which also includes ArrayBuffer and DataView. This makes the example incomplete and may imply that these types are not supported.

What did you expect to see?

Please update the example and/or surrounding text to mention that TextDecoder.decode() accepts a BufferSource, including ArrayBuffer, DataView, and all TypedArray types (such as Uint32Array).

For example:

const decoder = new TextDecoder();

// Uint32Array
const u32arr = new Uint32Array([3081674992]);
console.log(decoder.decode(u32arr)); // 𠮷

// ArrayBuffer
console.log(decoder.decode(u32arr.buffer)); // 𠮷

// DataView
console.log(decoder.decode(new DataView(u32arr.buffer))); // 𠮷

### Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

- WHATWG Encoding Standard: `TextDecoder` and its `decode()` method accept a `BufferSource`.
  https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-textdecoder

- Web IDL: `BufferSource` is defined as `(ArrayBufferView or ArrayBuffer)`. `ArrayBufferView` includes `DataView` and all `TypedArray` types, such as `Uint32Array`.
  https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#BufferSource


### Do you have anything more you want to share?

_No response_
items.title: [encoding] TextDecoder example should mention all BufferSource inputs: ArrayBuffer, DataView, and all TypedArrays including Uint32Array

items.content_html:
What is the new suggestion?

Webcodecs introduce ImageDecoder and ImageDecoder come with ImageTrackList.
It sounds like a nice feature but I can't figure out how to provide an image file containing multiple tracks...
I even never heard about tracks inside an image and google doesn't help me at all with that.

ImageTrackList exists so I'm sure it's doable but how to package multiple tracks inside a single image file ?

Why is it important or useful?

I think it would be a great way to organised assets compared to a spritesheet but I have no idea how to create the multi-tracks-image. What tool am I suppose to use ? What would be the format of the file ?

"Does it address critical needs in the web industry?"
Probably not but this feature existed in Adobe Flash (the ability to package multiple assets, easy to target, inside a single file) and I really miss it. The idea I could do it again soon with ImageDecoder & ImageTrackList makes me very happy. Please show us a step by step example to create such images .

MDN URL: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/
